title: AAC Coverage Report
description: A machine-readable conformance claim: which obligations a system covers, how, and with what evidence. Emitted by CI as a byproduct of testing — never hand-assembled — and consumed by release reviews, GRC platforms and auditors. See docs/REPORT.md for the semantics of a claim.

report_version.description: Version of THIS report format. Distinct from catalog_version — the format and the obligations evolve independently.

catalog_version.description: Catalog release this claim is made against. Required: without it the set of obligations being claimed is undefined and the report is not interpretable.

generated_at.description: When this report was produced. A report generated as a byproduct of a pipeline run is stronger evidence than one assembled for a review, and the timestamp series across commits is what demonstrates a control operates continuously.

profile.description: Named conformance profile, if the adopter uses one. Absent means the full applicable set.

subject.description: What is being claimed about. The archetype classification determines which obligations apply, so a coverage count without it is meaningless.

version.description: Release tag, commit SHA or build identifier.

archetypes.description: Every archetype present in the system. Most real systems are two or three composed.

results.description: One entry per APPLICABLE obligation. Silence is not a permitted answer — an obligation with no entry is indistinguishable from one nobody considered, which is exactly the ambiguity this format exists to remove. Use status 'not-covered' to say so honestly.

status.description: Whether a check EXISTS. Distinct from outcome, which is whether it passed — see docs/REPORT.md. 'not-covered' is the honest default for work not yet done.

outcome.description: Result of the most recent run. Only meaningful when status is 'covered'. A covered obligation whose outcome is 'fail' is a working control reporting a real problem — materially different from an obligation nobody checks.

mechanisms.description: Mechanisms actually used, which need not match the case's advisory tags.

evidence.description: Pointers a reviewer can follow. Required when status is 'covered' — a coverage claim with nothing behind it is an assertion, not evidence.

type.description: 'test' a runner identifier; 'experiment' an eval platform run; 'trace-query' a saved query over telemetry; 'policy' a gateway or guardrail rule; 'annotation' a human review batch; 'document' a sign-off record.

owner.description: Accountable person or team. Required for accepted-risk.

rationale.description: Why this status. Required for accepted-risk and not-applicable.

review_by.description: When an accepted risk is next reviewed. Required for accepted-risk: an acceptance without an expiry is an omission wearing a process.

summary.description: Optional and derived. A validator recomputes these from results and rejects a mismatch, so a report cannot claim a summary its own contents do not support.
